scope: ID CONTROL ACHIEVED and the 'id out of range' hypothesis FALSIFIED: id 8 is stored exactly as built, yet the client still ends at state 9 and exits

the_verification.verdict: EXACT - the assembly rule (byte163 bits 5-7 | byte165 << 3 | byte166 bit0 << 11) is confirmed and the id is now fully controllable

why_the_earlier_hypothesis_is_dead: round 228 proposed that id 4048 was out of range for the map and that a small id would let the client reach state 10
with id 8 - a value that is certainly in range for any map - the client still ends at state 9 and the process still exits
so the entity id is NOT what keeps the client on the loading screen
what_that_leaves_as_candidates: the entity block's own completion: with count > 0 the decoder reads an id and then a delta, and something in that path may leave the stream in a state the rest of the snapshot parser rejects
the client may require the entity to be a recognised player/actor (a valid eType) rather than merely present in the list
or the loading screen is waiting on a different message entirely (a clientNum/configstring tie) and the entity list is a red herring
what_is_now_solid: the entity list layout is exact: gates at bits 1307/1308, count as a byte at buffer[164], id as (byte163 bits 5-7 | byte165 << 3 | byte166 bit0 << 11)
and the id can be set to any 12-bit value deliberately - demonstrated by 4048 -> 8
next: use the now-working id control to test the 'recognised entity' idea: build an entity with a small id AND a mode-1 delta, and watch whether the client survives
in parallel, check whether the loading screen is gated on a clientNum or on a configstring the server is not setting
